item.title: Nick Bostrom on What Happens If AI Solves All Problems
item.description: The philosopher Nick Bostrom was one of the first thinkers who mapped out the existential risk of AI. In his 2014 book, Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies he delved into scenarios — like the “paperclip maximizer” for instance — that showed the dangers that unfettered and highly intelligent AI posed to humans. A decade later, in Deep Utopia: Life and Meaning in a Solved World, he looked at the other side of the AI coin, and theorizes what human experience might look like if AI is capable of solving all of our problems. What happens if AI and robots can literally do every single thing better than humans can? How would we find any meaning or satisfaction from life? On this episode, he speaks to us about the two divergent ways of understanding AI's future, what we might do, and what we can do right now to improve the chances that AI actually improves our lives. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Prepare Record Shareholder Returns
item.description: Samsung and SK Hynix are preparing record shareholder returns after investors sent their stocks tumbling over concerns around the sustainability of AI hardware spending. Bloomberg's Neil Campling has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hays Shifts to Hard-to-Replace Roles as AI Reshapes Hiring
item.description: Hays Plc will focus on hiring for roles that are harder to replace with artificial intelligence, as recruitment companies globally seek to mitigate the AI threat to the jobs market.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Gerace

item.title: SK Hynix Reaches Tentative Deal With Union on Wages, Yonhap Says
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. and its labor union have reached a tentative wage and collective bargaining agreement, featuring a 6.3% salary increase and a significant shift in how employee performance bonuses are apportioned, according to Yonhap News.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Why Are Chinese Citizens More Optimistic About AI Than Americans? Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about the gulf in AI optimism between the US and China in a Live Q&A on Friday, August 21, 2026 at 10 a.m. HKT.
item.dc:creator: Balazs Penz, Luz Ding, Alan Wong and Sunny Bangia

item.title: Thai PM’s Family Firm Eyes $1.5 Billion Data Center Bids
item.description: Stecon Group Pcl plans to bid for three data-center construction projects worth a combined 49.8 billion baht ($1.5 billion), betting on the sector to drive further growth as technology investment surges in Thailand.
item.dc:creator: Anuchit Nguyen

item.title: AI Startup Callosum Raises $100 Million to Make AI Tasks Cheaper
item.description: Callosum, a startup that makes software to match specific artificial intelligence tasks with different models and chips, has raised $100 million in early financing from backers including the UK’s public AI fund.
item.dc:creator: Anna Boyne and Mark Bergen

item.title: Convergence-Backed Comsol to Build New South Africa 5G Network
item.description: Comsol Networks Pty Ltd. is completing a multi-billion-rand debt and equity raise to build a new 5G network in South Africa, according to founder and Chief Executive Officer Iain Stevenson.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo

item.title: China's Xynova on Developing Human-like Robot Hands
item.description: Alex Xia, Founder and CEO at Hangzhou-based robot hand maker Xynova, discusses innovation and industry bottlenecks. He also talks about and fundraising plans exclusively on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LeadShine's Zheng on China's Robotics Supply Chain
item.description: Nangle Zheng, Strategic Investment Director at LeadShine Technology, says China has shortened the development cycle for humanoid robots from years to just months. He speaks to David Ingles and Yvonne Man on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Unitree Sees Robots Reaching ‘Mass Market’ Within Decade
item.description: Humanoid robots will reach “mass market” popularity within a decade, after manufacturers solve problems that hold back their current usefulness, the founder of China’s Unitree Robotics said.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AIA CFO on 1H26 Results
item.description: Garth Jones, CFO of AIA Group, discusses the Hong Kong-listed insurer's 13% growth in value of new business in the first half of the year. He says the fundamental demand for business remains in China, but the company is also looking to continue to invest in ASEAN region, as it is a core growth engine. He speaks exclusively with Paul Allen on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Evolution Mining CEO on Earnings, Deals outlook
item.description: Lawrie Conway, Managing Director and CEO of Evolution Mining, discusses the miner's full-year profit that saw a 59% growth year on year. He also discusses the company's dividend payout plans and potential acquisitions. He speaks with Paul Allen on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Camera-Equipped AI AirPods Remain on Track for 2027 Despite Video Leak
item.description: An Apple Inc. effort to sell camera-equipped AirPods remains on track for 2027, despite a leak from the company indicating that the product might arrive sooner.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Labubu Maker Set For Drastic Growth Slowdown as Bears Gather
item.description: Pop Mart International Group Ltd. is poised to report a sharp slowdown in first-half sales growth Thursday, raising the stakes for a company that has lost roughly $32 billion in market value since the peak of Labubu mania.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Markets Rebound as Treasury Moves to Rein In Yields | The Close 8/19/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are JPMorgan Private Bank Head of Alternative Investment Strategy Sitara Sundar, Ramp Co-Founder & Co-CEO Eric Glyman, D.A. Davidson Managing Director Senior Research Analyst Michael Baker, The Estée Lauder Companies President & CEO Stéphane de La Faverie, Neuberger Senior Portfolio Manager Eli Salzmann, PGIM Public & Private Fixed Income Co-Chief Investment Officer Gregory Peters, Gravis Robotics CEO & Co-Founder Ryan Luke Johns, Former Walgreens Boots Alliance CEO Roz Brewer, & LSEG Consumer Research Director Jharrone Martis. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PGIM’s Greg Peters on Bessent’s Debt Buyback Boost
item.description: Greg Peters, Co-CIO of Public and Private Fixed Income at PGIM, discussed the Treasury's recent decision to boost debt buybacks for 10-year to 30-year securities. The cap on buybacks has been doubled from $2 billion to $4 billion, reflecting an aggressive move to manage the debt portfolio. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Chip Startup Fractile in Talks for $6.5 Billion Value After Anthropic Deal
item.description: Fractile, a startup developing chips tailored for artificial intelligence use that has a deal to supply Anthropic PBC, is in advanced talks to notch a valuation more than six times higher than the price it landed in May.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Dina Bass

item.title: SK Hynix Moves to Calm Market With $29 Billion Share Buyback
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. unveiled plans to buy back 40 trillion won ($29 billion) of stock and return more profits to investors, moving to stabilize its shares after they fell more than 50% in two months.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Denny Thomas

item.title: Alphabet Sells Long Aussie Bond With Record Yield Near 7%
item.description: Alphabet Inc. paid just under 7% to borrow longer-dated funds in its debut Australian dollar bond offering, its highest-ever for a note, underscoring how broader demands for cash among hyperscalers around the world are feeding into more costly funding almost everywhere.
item.dc:creator: Finbarr Flynn, Matthew Burgess and Sharon Klyne
